Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Alexander Maclaren (author, Wikidata Q4719516), died 1910; William Robertson Nicoll (editor, Wikidata Q8017677), died 1923. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Maclaren, Alexander, 1826-1910; Nicoll, W. Robertson (William Robertson), Sir, 1851-1923 [Editor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The Epistles of St. Paul to the Colossians and Philemon, New York : A.C. Armstrong, 1897, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/epistlesofstpaul0000macl. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 100%, 89%, 84% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of William Robertson Nicoll, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
